senses.gloss:
ऋश्य ऋश्य or ऋश, अस्, m. the male of a
species of antelope, the painted or white-footed ante-
lope; [cf. ऋष्य and रिश्य.]
—ऋश्य-केतु, उस्, m.
an epithet of Aniruddha; (a various reading for विश्व-
केतु.)
—ऋश्य-द, अस्, m. (द fr. rt. 4. दा, ‘to bind’),
a pit for catching antelopes.
—ऋश्य-पद्, आत्, अदी,
अत्, Ved. having the feet of an antelope.

ऋष्य ऋष्य, अस्, m. [cf. ऋश्य], the painted
or white-footed antelope; N. of a son of Devātithi;
(अम्), n. a kind of leprosy.
—ऋष्य-केतन, अस्, and
ऋष्य-केतु, उस्, m., N. of Aniruddha.
—ऋष्य-
गता, f. the plant Asparagus Racemosus.
—ऋष्य-
गन्धा, f. the plant Convolvulus Argenteus.
—ऋष्य-
जिह्व, अम्, n. a kind of leprosy.
—ऋष्य-प्रोक्ता,
f., N. of several plants, Carpopogon Pruriens, Aspa-
ragus Racemosus, Sida Cordifolia or Rhombifolia.
—ऋष्य-मूक, अस्, m. a mountain in the Dekhan,
the temporary abode of Rāma with the monkey-chief
[]
Sugrīva.
—ऋष्य-शृङ्ग, अस्, m., N. of a personage
(son of the Ṛṣi Vibhāṇḍaka) whose story is told in
Rāmāyaṇa. 1. 9; N. of a legislator.
—ऋष्याङ्क
(˚य-अङ्˚), अस्, m. an epithet of Aniruddha.

ऋष्यक, अस्, m. the painted or white-footed
antelope.
